label: Presence, inert emptiness and a possible contingent-free past refute accessible deletion (inference)
rule: Compose InertEmptiness.earlierNecessary at the witness history; apply deletion there to its necessary individual
meaning: Conditional incompatibility, non-transcription, composed from InertEmptiness.earlierNecessary. The possible contingent-free past gives an accessible history v; presence-to-existence and inert emptiness give a concrete individual c existing at v and necessary relative to v; deletion at v would put c's absence at a world accessible from v. So the three non-frame premises of Arrival A (ActualEuclidean.inertNecessaryConcrete) are jointly inconsistent with deletion at every world accessible from w, a fortiori with worldwise deletion. Neither actual reflexivity nor Euclidean access is used. Deletion at w alone is not enough: OriginToleranceIdentity.Control.faithful satisfies the three premises and deletion at actual (OriginDeletion.Control.Certificate, group 1). This refutes the strengthened bundle only; it does not make the original countermodel vacuous and establishes none of the premises.
